config.description: v028's exact recipe -- same architecture, same distill_weight 1.0, same teacher, same seed -- with ONE change: training.epochs 3 -> 5. 225,922 params, so the latency profile is identical to v028 and inherited by construction.
config.hypothesis:
The local-to-public offset is NOT a constant, and it moves with training length. Measured across six scored submissions, five 3-epoch runs share an offset of -0.028264 +/- 0.000419. v025 -- the only 5-epoch run -- sits at -0.026438, which is +0.001826 from that mean, or +4.4 sigma. The control is unusually clean: v024 is the SAME recipe as v025 at 3 epochs and sits normally at -0.028818, so batch 64 is exonerated and epochs is the only structural difference. Against v024 specifically the shift is +0.002380.
The consequence is that full_valid_wp is a BIASED selector across different training lengths, biased against the longer run. v025 was ranked a -1.5 sigma local regression and was therefore nearly discarded, yet it scored 0.6580 public and beat v023 (0.6568) by +0.0012. Local selection actively mis-ranked it.
So combine the two things that are known to help. v028 has the best local score in the project (0.686510, +11.5 sigma) and carries the standard offset. v025 demonstrates a +0.0024 public uplift from training longer. If the two compose, the prediction is 0.6585 + 0.0024 = 0.6609, against a 0.6711 leader where we currently sit 0.0092 back.
Falsifiable and stated as such: this predicts a public score near 0.6609. If the run instead lands at v028's 0.6585, the epoch effect did not transfer to this recipe and the offset shift was specific to v025's lower distillation weight -- which would be a genuinely interesting distinction, since it would mean the two levers interact rather than add.
config.change_vs_parent: training.epochs 3 -> 5 only. distill_weight stays 1.0, gamma stays absent, params, hidden, input_proj, chunk_len, teacher, schedule, LR and seed are all unchanged, so this isolates training length against v028 rather than against v025.
